title: Home Fries
subtitle: Pan-fried diced potatoes with onion and peppers
excerpt: Home fries are pan-fried diced or sliced potatoes cooked with onion and peppers until crispy on the outside and tender inside. They are the American diner alternative to hash browns: chunkier, with more texture, and usually including onion and pepper as integral parts of the dish.
sourceNotes: Home fries are a staple of American diner breakfast cooking. Unlike hash browns (shredded potato) or French fries (deep-fried), home fries are cooked in a frying pan with relatively little fat. They are made from leftover boiled or parboiled potatoes in traditional versions.

recipe.batchNotes: Cook extra parboiled potatoes the night before for fast home fries in the morning.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Parboil and cool the potatoes the evening before. Finish in the pan in the morning.

content.text: Home fries work best when the potato is parboiled first: cooked in salted water for 8 to 10 minutes until barely tender, then cooled and diced. Cold, parboiled potato has lost most of its surface starch, which means it will brown properly in the pan rather than stick and steam. Raw diced potato takes much longer to cook through and the outside tends to char before the inside is done.

items.prepNote: any variety, parboiled, cooled, and diced into 1.5 cm cubes

content.text: Heat the oil in a cast-iron pan or large frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the diced parboiled potatoes in a single layer. Do not stir for 4 to 5 minutes until the undersides are deeply golden. Turn and cook for a further 4 to 5 minutes.
Add the onion and red pepper. Toss together and cook for a further 8 to 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the onion is softened and the potatoes are evenly golden.
Sprinkle over the paprika and garlic powder and season generously with salt and pepper. Toss to coat and cook for 1 minute more.

items.symptom: Potatoes are sticking and not browning
items.cause: Pan not hot enough, or potatoes moved too soon before a crust formed
items.fix: Resist stirring for at least 4 to 5 minutes after the potatoes go in. A cast-iron pan or heavy non-stick pan gives better results than thin stainless steel.
